papers.what_it_is: A theory-and-simulation paper that defines quantum Gaussian processes (Bayesian priors over unknown quantum transformations), proves that matchgate (free-fermionic) evolutions give provable and scalable QGPs acting on all qubits, and demonstrates regression, classification and Bayesian optimization in MPS simulations of up to 100 qubits.

existing.value: The authors report a 50-qubit synthetic regression task in which 15 training states with t in [0, 1] pass through an unknown random matchgate circuit and a Pauli observable in B1 is measured, with the signal to be predicted out to t ≤ 10; with the wrong prior (the unitary kernel, as if U could be any unitary) extrapolation is unattainable, while with the correct matchgate kernel the QGP extrapolates perfectly without shot noise and remains robust with realistic finite shots, which broaden the uncertainty bands. They conclude that interpolation can generally be achieved but extrapolation becomes impossible without a suitable inductive bias.

papers.what_it_is: A theoretical and numerical study of the long-time-average Krylov spread complexity of continuous-time quantum walks on graphs, relating it to the quantum-walk limiting distribution and finding graphs of minimal and maximal complexity.
